name: eth_signature_mmd_regime_sizing_overlay_20260811
created: 2026-08-11, written BEFORE the higherOrderKME dependency was confirmed to install and BEFORE any Signature-MMD number was computed
status: OPENED -- blocked on IG0 (dependency check). No script exists yet.
question: Does a Signature-MMD path-clustering regime signal (Horvath & Issa, arXiv:2306.15835, github.com/issaz/signature-regime-detection) carry information about h48qual trade OUTCOME VARIANCE/DRAWDOWN that the existing JM/wide24 regime detectors do not, when used as a position-SIZING overlay -- NOT as a classification input feature.

scope_and_framing.why_sizing_and_not_a_14th_classification: This line was explicitly separated from the same-day 13-feature h48qual input-feature contract (cvp_regime, funding_roc_288, funding_pressure_diff1, ou_halflife, m7_vae_error_dt288, long_squeeze_risk_dt288, whale_retail_ratio_dt288, fvg_dist, realized_skewness, sum_toptrader_long_short_ratio_dt288, breakout_strength, session_japan, eth_vol_risk_premium). This project's own prior literature review (docs/entry_exit_edge_root_cause_and_literature_review_20260809.md) already categorizes Signature-MMD as a SIZING-overlay regime-detector candidate, not an entry/quality-classification candidate. Running it through the F-test/MI-vs-shuffled-null pipeline used for the 13 features would test it for the wrong job.
scope_and_framing.why_not_redundant_with_JM: JM (scripts/build_*_regime3_jm_lam4_20260809.py and the 20260810 redesign) fits a k=3 jump-penalized clustering on a HAND-SELECTED SUMMARY-STATISTIC feature vector (bb_width, rsi, mtf_trend_4h, kalman_velocity, ...), i.e. a Markovian snapshot: the state depends only on the current feature vector, and any path-order information within the lookback window is already lost by the time it reaches the clustering step. Signature-MMD instead transforms the raw PATH itself (price/volume over a window) via iterated-integral signatures and compares path segments with a kernel two-sample test (MMD) -- explicitly designed for non-Markovian, path-dependent structure. The two methods can disagree in a way that is informative, not merely redundant, precisely because they see different representations of the same underlying process.
scope_and_framing.why_expectations_should_still_be_tempere: The same-day input-feature analysis (13-feature contract above) found that even a corrected TabM ensemble barely beats a constant-frequency baseline (VAL logloss within 0.0001-0.0003 of baseline) predicting the h48qual triple-barrier outcome from 13 statistically-validated features. If the 5-minute barrier race is close to intrinsically noisy at this horizon, a richer regime representation may not raise that ceiling even if it captures genuinely different information about price dynamics -- this contract tests a SIZING claim (does variance/MDD differ by regime), which is a lower bar than a DIRECTION claim, but it is not a free pass from the same underlying noise floor.

implementation_gates.purpose: None of the pre_registered_gates below can be written with real numbers until these three sequential technical go/no-go checks clear. This section exists so a future session does not have to re-derive the plan from conversation history.

IG0_dependency_check.rule: `higherOrderKME` (the signature-kernel MMD package the reference implementation depends on) must install and import cleanly in the quant_ai conda env.
IG0_dependency_check.known_risk: The repo's own README warns: 'some users may have issues installing higherOrderKME... conflicts with older h5py versions.'
IG0_dependency_check.on_fail: HALT this contract. Before abandoning the axis, check whether a plain `iisignature`/`signatory` signature computation plus a hand-rolled RBF-kernel MMD two-sample statistic can reproduce the paper's detection test without the specialized package -- record that decision as a contract revision, do not silently substitute methods.

IG1_algorithm_confirmation.rule: Read the paper's online/causal regime-CHANGE-detection algorithm (Sections 4.1-4.4 -- NOT Section 5's offline regime-clustering algorithm, which the paper itself frames as an ex-ante historical-analysis tool, not a live signal) directly from `src/` and the matching notebook, not from a summarized fetch. Confirm: raw input channels (price only, or price+volume), window/lookback length used in the paper's crypto experiment (Section 6), and output type (continuous MMD score vs. discrete regime-change flag vs. cluster ID).
IG1_algorithm_confirmation.on_fail: If the online-detection variant cannot be made to run bar-by-bar without seeing data beyond its own causal window, this axis produces no usable live feature and should be closed here -- do not adapt the offline clustering algorithm into a pseudo-causal form by re-fitting it on an expanding window and calling that 'causal'; that reintroduces the exact lookback-into-history bias the paper's online variant exists to avoid.

IG2_causal_pilot_fit.rule: A pilot fit on ETH's actual 5m price/volume path produces a well-defined signal under this project's existing fresh_forward discipline (see the `fresh_forward` block below) -- no full-history lookback, no future rows, walk-forward only.
IG2_causal_pilot_fit.on_fail: HALT. Document why (e.g. compute cost per bar too high for 5m cadence, window length requires more history than available pre-2024).

supporting.jm_oos_instability: The 2026-08-10 JM regime redesign showed economic-separation t-stat flipping sign OOS for ETH (VAL t=+2.44 -> OOS t=-2.58) despite strong classification accuracy -- evidence that the current Markovian/summary-statistic regime representation has a real, demonstrated weakness that a structurally different (path-dependent) method might or might not address.
supporting.paper_own_validation: The paper's abstract states its clustering tools, applied to real cryptocurrency data, 'accurately indicated historical periods of market turmoil' -- an ex-post claim about the offline clustering variant specifically, not yet evidence for the causal online variant this contract requires (see IG1).

ADVERSE -- this contract expects a hard.sizing_overlay_track_record_in_this_repo: The BTC czz_trend regime-sizing overlay -- structurally the closest precedent to what this contract proposes -- was adopted on a paired time-block bootstrap P=0.739 and later downgraded to NOT-SUPPORTED / shadow-only when an audit found its per-trade effect was t=-0.99 (p=0.33) and its risk channel pointed the wrong way (variance ratio 0.881, i.e. it downsized the LESS volatile bucket). This is exactly why schema v3's effect_size_gate exists and is pre-declared below rather than left for later.
ADVERSE -- this contract expects a hard.dependency_risk: higherOrderKME's documented install friction (IG0) is a real chance this axis closes before producing a single number.
